evals.name: module-local-order-transaction
evals.prompt: Model order cancellation inside an order Business Module. Cancellation must enforce order status transitions, line-item consistency, and a payment-refund policy in one module-local transaction. Design the domain concepts and the smallest Unit of Work port, expose an admin CancelOrder contract, define ORDER_NOT_FOUND and ORDER_CANNOT_CANCEL as stable reasons, and add focused tests. Client messages must be localized only at the API edge.
evals.expected_output: A cohesive order module with explicit invariants, a module-local Unit of Work boundary, language-free domain errors, API error mapping/localization, and focused passing tests without distributed-transaction infrastructure.
expectations: The domain exists because concrete invariants and policies justify it, and it remains owned by the order Business Module.
Order, line item, status transition, and refund policy concepts are represented explicitly rather than as an ID-only entity.
The use case depends on the smallest order-owned Unit of Work port needed to commit its changes atomically.
Persistence tags and database-library types stay outside domain entities and ports.
ORDER_NOT_FOUND and ORDER_CANNOT_CANCEL remain stable machine-readable reasons; localization happens at the API edge.
No saga, Outbox, Inbox, remote client, or cross-module transaction abstraction is added without a Process boundary.
